title: Partner integration SLO onboarding — ops kit & 6-week sprint plan
content:
Purpose:
This working kit outlines the cross-functional plan to onboard external partner integrations (third-party connectors and partner-hosted endpoints) into Redwood's SLO program. Goal is to define measurable SLOs, ensure observability, automate alerting, and provide safe rollout controls across Product, Platform, Serving Runtime, and SRE teams.

Context & problem statement:
- Increasing number of partner integrations (file storage, identity providers, telemetry forwarders) have been deployed with inconsistent monitoring signals and unclear behavioral SLIs.
- Some integrations manifest as transient latency spikes or partial errors (400/422), which are currently routed to partner owners with limited instrumentation.
- Without consistent SLOs and runbooks we lack predictable incident behavior and cannot tie reliability investments to customer-facing outcomes or error budgets.

Scope (in-scope / out-of-scope):
- In-scope: partner connectors used by hosted API customers and Redwood Dedicated clusters; metrics collection, SLIs/SLOs definition, dashboards, alerting, and rollout/rollback playbooks.
- Out-of-scope: internal-only integrations, vendor contract negotiation, model-level quality SLOs (handled by product-ml).

Key stakeholders & RACI (summary):
- Eng-SRE (owner): define platform SLI schemas, templates for dashboards, alerting thresholds, onboarding checklist, runbook review.
- Platform-Engineering (accountable): ensure telemetry collection & metric namespaces, deploy exporters, cloud infra changes.
- Serving-Runtime (consulted): provide guidance on sampling, latency buckets, and buffer/queue metrics.
- Product-Hosted-API (consulted): set customer-facing SLO targets and acceptance criteria.
- Solutions/Customer Success (informed): readiness for customer comms and on-call handoff.

Top-level success criteria (what done looks like):
1) Every partnered integration has a documented SLI/SLO file in the monitoring repo (standard YAML schema) + owner contact.
2) Dashboards (per-integration & aggregate) exist in Grafana, with 90th/95th/99th latency panels and error-rate panels.
3) Alerts mapped to runbooks with clear incident triggers and step-by-step remediation including partner contact escalation.
4) 6-week pilot with 3 partner integrations completed; error budget burn observable and one retro with cost/effort estimates for scale.

Proposed SLIs & example SLOs (templates):
- Availability SLI: successful request ratio (2xx / total requests) computed per 5m window. Example SLO: 99.9% success rate per rolling 30d for critical connectors.
- Latency SLI: p95 request latency for partner-facing RPCs, excluding cold-start buckets. Example SLO: p95 < 200ms for best-effort connectors; p95 < 50ms for latency-sensitive endpoints.
- Partial-failure SLI: proportion of responses with partial results (status=206 or body.partial=true). Example SLO: partial responses < 0.5% monthly.
- Integration-specific SLI: downstream partner error rate (3xx/4xx/5xx from partner). SLO: downstream 5xx < 0.1% daily.

Instrumentation & data model (high level):
- Metric namespaces: integration.*.requests, integration.*.latency_ms_histogram, integration.*.partial_responses, integration.*.downstream_5xx_count.
- Tagging: service, integration_name, region, model_variant(optional), route.
- Recommended retention: high-cardinality metrics for 30 days, histograms and aggregated counters for 90 days.
- Traces: sample 1% of requests with full tracing; increase to 10% during incident windows via dynamic sampling.

6-week sprint plan (high level):
Week 0 (Prep): finalize YAML schema, onboard a monitoring repo template, runbook template, stakeholder kickoff.
Week 1: Platform engineers enable exporters and metric collection for pilot integration A; SRE implements dashboard template and baseline queries.
Week 2: Serving runtime validates latency buckets and tagging; product sets SLO targets for integration A; create alerts and runbook draft.
Week 3: Pilot integration A enters soft rollout to 10% traffic with alerting enabled; observe error budget burn and adjust thresholds.
Week 4: Repeat for integration B (different partner tech stack) — platform + SRE iterate on schema issues discovered.
Week 5: Integration C (higher-traffic) onboarding; create aggregate dashboards and cross-integration rollup.
Week 6: Pilot wrap-up, final runbooks, executive summary, retro, and proposal for org-wide rollout.

Per-sprint deliverables checklist (for each integration):
- metric ingestion verification (raw counters and histogram samples)
- SLI queries committed to monitoring repo
- Grafana dashboard created from template
- Alert rules created and tested in staging (with alerting suppression for soft rollout)
- Runbook reviewed and owner assigned
- On-call escalation matrix updated

Runbook example (abridged):
Trigger: integration_name success_rate < SLO_threshold for 15m AND error-rate delta > 2x baseline.
Immediate steps:
1) Pager goes to integration owner + SRE primary.
2) Check last 60m trends (dashboard): request rate, error class breakdown, latency histogram.
3) If downstream partner 5xx spike: contact partner on-call, enable retry/backoff ramp, activate circuit-breaker if available.
4) If increase due to config rollout: rollback config toggle; check canary percentages.
5) Declare incident if customer-impacting or error budget forecast < 48h at current burn rate.

Risk mitigation & fallback patterns:
- Circuit breakers & graceful degradation: recommend default behavior to return cached responses or soft-fail instead of blocking client requests.
- Fallback model variants: route to more robust model variant when partner timeouts exceed threshold.
- Rate-limiting & quota protection: apply temporary throttles per-integration to protect core runtime.

Measurement & reporting cadence:
- Daily: SRE runbook owner sanity check for pilot integrations (automated health email).
- Weekly: reliability sync with product and platform to review error budget burn and capacity concerns.
- Monthly: executive report summarizing SLO attainment, incidents, and operational cost.

Pilot selection guidance (to pick the 3 pilots):
- Choose varied tech stacks (HTTP webhooks, gRPC, SFTP) to flush out instrumentation gaps.
- At least one high-traffic integration used by Dedicated customers.
- At least one partner-managed endpoint to validate downstream error visibility.

Open questions & TODOs (working list):
- Decide exact sampling policy for traces in production (SRE + serving runtime).
- Agreement on SLO targets for best-effort vs critical integrations (product).
- Storage & retention cost estimate for histograms at scale (finance/infra).
- Automation: reduce onboarding from days to hours with a CLI or GitHub blueprint (engineering).

Appendix: standard YAML schema snippet (example lines):
- name: integration_name
  owner: team@example.com
  slos:
    - id: availability_v1
      description: "2xx success ratio (30d)"
      sli: "sum(integration.${name}.success) / sum(integration.${name}.requests)"
      target: "0.999"
      window: "30d"

Next steps (for this doc):
- Review with Platform-Engineering + Product on 2025-05-12 (stakeholder sync).
- Assign first three pilot owners by 2025-05-16.
- Create monitoring repo PR with templates by 2025-05-23.

Notes to reviewers: this is an operational working draft, expect iterative clarifications. Add feedback inline or tag issues in the monitoring repo.
